evidence.claim: The 800G to 1.6T datacenter optical transition can move bottlenecks across InP wafers, lasers, photodiodes, optical manufacturing services, and module assembly.
New orders for MOCVD, ion-beam deposition, and other compound semiconductor photonics tools can serve as early signals that optical component suppliers are adding capacity for AI data-center demand.

memory_update.text: AXTI mapped to the InP wafer substrate node as an underfollowed material-level AI photonics candidate; evidence remains inference-level until filings confirm AI/datacenter InP backlog, customer qualification, and revenue conversion.
VECO mapped to the compound semiconductor photonics equipment node; tool orders could act as early capacity-expansion signals for AI optical devices, but durability of the cycle must be verified.
FN mapped to specialized optical manufacturing services for 800G/1.6T AI datacenter interconnects; verify datacom AI mix, capacity, backlog, and customer concentration.
6239.TW mapped as a hypothesis for memory-backend OSAT overflow from AI/HBM crowding-out; requires Taiwan primary-source validation of AI/HPC packaging exposure and IDM outsourcing.
COHR and LITE retained as reference optical leaders to benchmark InP capacity, datacenter optical demand, and whether the bottleneck is at substrate, device, manufacturing, or module level.
AVGO retained as a reference demand anchor for custom AI accelerators and AI networking; provided context supports a fact-level link to custom AI silicon growth.

CRDO mapped as an underfollowed second-order AI bandwidth candidate through active electrical cables, retimers, and connectivity silicon; evidence remains hypothesis-level pending customer and design-win verification.
ALAB retained as a reference growth benchmark for AI server connectivity rather than as an underfollowed discovery candidate because attention and market expectations may already be high.

ALMU mapped only as a speculative shadow candidate for III-V-on-silicon photonics substitution if native InP capacity becomes constrained; commercial qualification and cash runway are gating evidence.

Primary-source verification is still needed for AXTI, VECO, FN, 6239.TW, COHR, LITE, CRDO, ALAB, and ALMU company-specific AI revenue mix, backlog, capacity, customer concentration, and margin claims.
Market-pricing checks are not yet performed for this chunk; next layer should compare market cap, valuation, analyst attention, short interest, and recent performance against evidence strength.

summary: This Layer 2B maps the candidate chunk into ticker-to-node relationships for AI infrastructure chokepoints, with the strongest direct relationships around optical interconnects, InP/compound-semiconductor photonics capacity, optical manufacturing services, memory-backend/advanced-packaging overflow, and high-speed connectivity silicon. Reference leaders such as COHR, LITE, AVGO, and ALAB are retained as demand anchors or benchmark comparables, while the main underfollowed lane focuses on AXTI, VECO, FN, 6239.TW, and CRDO. Evidence quality is intentionally conservative: company-specific claims not directly supported by the provided search context are labeled inference or hypothesis and require primary-source validation in later layers.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Check AXTI latest 10-Q/10-K, earnings call transcript, segment revenue by substrate type, InP commentary, backlog language, customer concentration, China/export-permit risk, capex, and utilization.
ticker_relationships.node: InP wafer substrates and compound semiconductor substrates for AI datacenter photonics
ticker_relationships.relationship: AXT is mapped as an upstream substrate supplier candidate for InP-dependent optical devices used in 800G/1.6T datacenter optical links. If AI optical interconnect demand tightens native InP wafer supply, AXTI could be closer to the material bottleneck than module-level optical names.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify whether 2026 InP equipment orders represent one-time capacity catch-up or a durable multi-year photonics capex cycle.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Check VECO latest filings, order backlog, book-to-bill, photonics/compound-semiconductor revenue disclosures, customer capex references, and management language on AI datacenter optical demand.
ticker_relationships.node: Compound semiconductor and photonics manufacturing equipment
ticker_relationships.relationship: Veeco is mapped as an upstream tool supplier whose MOCVD, ion-beam deposition, or related compound-semiconductor equipment orders could serve as early evidence of capacity expansion for InP lasers, photodiodes, and other optical devices used in AI datacenter interconnects.

ticker_relationships.node: Specialized optical manufacturing services for 800G/1.6T transceivers
ticker_relationships.relationship: Fabrinet is mapped as a specialized manufacturing platform that may benefit when AI cluster bandwidth demand increases outsourced production of optical components and modules. The relationship is second-order because Fabrinet may depend on customer ramps, qualification gates, and available Thailand capacity rather than owning the optical component IP itself.

The hypothesis is that AI-driven HBM demand may crowd out conventional DRAM/NAND backend capacity at memory IDMs, pushing incremental packaging and test work to third-party OSATs.
